_meta.purpose: Lexical & well-formedness knowledge base the AI fix suggester consults to detect and repair SYNTACTIC errors that the global business KB does NOT cover: stray characters, unwanted commas/spaces, unescaped special characters (& < > " '), invisible/control/zero-width characters, encoding artifacts (smart quotes, NBSP, BOM), whitespace contamination, malformed numbers/amounts (thousands separators, currency symbols), malformed date/time separators, namespace/prefix syntax, and XML structural well-formedness (unclosed/mismatched/overlapping tags, bad attribute quoting, undefined entities). These are the faults that break parsing or lexical validation BEFORE schema/business validation can even run. This KB is COMPLEMENTARY to the global SWIFT/business KB and must never duplicate or override its element/codelist/dependency rules.
_meta.companion_kb: Global SWIFT CBPR+ business/XSD KB v2.1 (field_constraints, error_code_catalogue, dependencies, tag_templates).
_meta.golden_rule: Always FIX the syntax of an existing value in place; never invent a new business value to paper over a syntax fault. Stripping a stray comma, escaping an &, or trimming a space must PRESERVE the original intended content. Only after this KB's repairs leave the document well-formed should the global business KB be consulted.

scope_and_precedence._doc: Defines what this KB owns, what it must not touch, and the order in which a fixer applies it relative to the global KB.
this_kb_owns: Character-level contamination (illegal, invisible, control, zero-width, smart/curly, accented in strict fields)
Entity escaping of the five XML predefined characters (& < > " ')
Whitespace contamination (leading, trailing, internal, newline/tab, pretty-print leakage, empty elements)
Numeric & amount lexical form (thousands separators, decimal comma, currency symbols, spaces, signs, scientific notation)
Date/time lexical form (separator characters, spacing, missing 'T') — the LEXICAL shape only
Encoding declaration and byte-level integrity (BOM, UTF-8 validity)
this_kb_must_not_touch: Whether an element is mandatory/optional (global KB: MISSING_MANDATORY_FIELD, cbpr_plus_rules.mandatory_fields)
Codelist membership (global KB: SCHEMENAME_INVALID, ChrgBr/SttlmMtd/TxSts etc.)
Cross-field equality/dependency (global KB: BIZMSGIDR_EQ_GRPHDR_MSGID, NBOFTXS, CtrlSum, Fr/To==agent)
BIC/IBAN registry or checksum validity (global KB: INVALID_BICFI, IBAN_INVALID) — though LENGTH/whitespace/charset of those values IS in scope here

Business 'Z-forbidden' / milliseconds datetime rules (global KB: CBPR_DATETIME_Z_FORBIDDEN, CBPR_DATETIME_MILLISECONDS) — this KB only fixes lexical separators/spacing; it cross-references those codes, never re-decides them
fix_pipeline_order: 1. BYTE/ENCODING PASS — resolve BOM, encoding-declaration mismatch, invalid UTF-8 bytes (file will not parse otherwise).
3. WELL-FORMEDNESS PASS — escape & < > " '; fix unclosed/mismatched/overlapping tags, attribute quoting, undefined entities, comments/CDATA, stray text, multiple roots.
4. WHITESPACE PASS — trim leading/trailing, strip internal whitespace from strict tokens, fix pretty-print leakage, empty/whitespace-only elements.
5. VALUE-LEXICAL PASS — normalise amounts (remove thousands separators/currency symbols/spaces), numbers, and date/time separators.
6. NAMESPACE/ATTRIBUTE PASS — undeclared prefixes, close-tag prefix mismatch, attribute lexical form (e.g. Ccy casing/spacing).
7. HANDOFF — only once the document is well-formed and lexically clean, pass control to the GLOBAL business KB for schema/codelist/dependency fixes.
scope_and_precedence.critical_note: If a fault is BOTH syntactic and business (e.g. an amount with a thousands separator that, once cleaned, also has too many decimals), this KB only removes the separator; the decimal-precision/business judgement belongs to the global KB (R12 / D00007). Hand off cleanly; do not double-fix.

detection_strategy._doc: How the AI should hunt for syntactic faults. Scan in this order and report every hit; do not stop at the first.
steps: Read the raw bytes BEFORE XML parsing: check for a UTF-8 BOM (EF BB BF), other BOMs (FF FE / FE FF / 00 00 FE FF), and any byte that is not valid UTF-8.
Confirm the very first bytes (after any BOM you decide to keep/strip) are '<?xml' or '<'; any character — including a space, blank line, or stray text — before the XML declaration is fatal.
Scan every TEXT NODE and every ATTRIBUTE VALUE for the raw characters & < > and, inside attribute values, the active quote character; each unescaped occurrence is a well-formedness fault.

Scan every character of every text node and attribute value against the Unicode blocklist (control, zero-width, smart quotes, NBSP, dashes, ellipsis, soft hyphen); flag any non-ASCII or non-printable code point and decide per field-class whether to transliterate, escape, or strip.
For each element, classify it by field_class (strict_token / identifier / numeric_amount / datetime / text) and apply that class's whitespace and character policy.
For amounts and numbers, check for grouping separators, currency symbols, spaces, signs, and non-dot decimal marks.
For dates/datetimes, check the separator characters and the date/time delimiter ('T') — LEXICAL only.
Verify tag nesting with a stack: every start tag must have a matching, correctly-cased, correctly-nested end tag; every attribute must be quoted once; no duplicate attributes; no undefined entities.
Check namespace prefixes used vs declared, and that close-tag prefixes match open-tag prefixes.
Check for anything after the single root element's close tag.
detection_strategy.reporting: Emit one finding per distinct fault with: error_code (from this KB's error_code_catalogue), the offending xpath or byte offset, the exact offending character/sequence (quoted), and the deterministic fix.

field_class_policy._doc: Every element value falls into one class. The class dictates the whitespace and character rules this KB enforces. Element-to-class mapping examples are illustrative, not exhaustive.

strict_token.description: No whitespace anywhere (not leading, trailing, or internal). Restricted character set. A single stray space or hidden character makes the value invalid.
strict_token.whitespace: FORBIDDEN entirely. Trim and strip all spaces, tabs, newlines, NBSP, zero-width.
strict_token.charset: Per-type (see global field_constraints). No punctuation beyond the type's own grammar (e.g. '-' and ':' in datetimes, '.' in amounts).

identifier.description: FIN-X character set, no leading/trailing whitespace; internal spaces are generally invalid for ID fields and must be removed (global KB notes 'No spaces' for MsgId/BizMsgIdr).
identifier.whitespace: No leading/trailing. Internal spaces: remove (or replace with '-') — they are not part of the intended reference.
identifier.charset: FIN-X: A-Z a-z 0-9 / - ? : ( ) . , ' + and SPACE. Anything else (e.g. @ # % & < > " *) is a charset fault; escape if it is one of the XML-special five, otherwise strip/transliterate.

numeric_amount.description: Decimal number; dot is the ONLY decimal separator; no grouping separators; no currency symbol; no spaces; no leading '+'.
numeric_amount.charset: [0-9] and at most one '.'; optional leading '-' only where the schema allows negatives (most ISO amounts are non-negative).

datetime.description: ISO 8601 lexical shape. This KB fixes ONLY the separator/spacing shape; the Z/offset/milliseconds business rules belong to the global KB.
datetime.whitespace: FORBIDDEN. No space between date and time — use 'T'.
datetime.charset: Date: YYYY-MM-DD with '-' separators only. DateTime: date + 'T' + HH:MM:SS + offset. Slash/dot separators and spaces are lexical faults.

text.description: Human-readable fields using the CBPR+ EXTENDED character set. These MAY legitimately contain & < > and other symbols, but those MUST be XML-escaped. Accented Latin letters are allowed in CBPR+ Nm/Adr/RmtInf, but invisible/smart/zero-width characters are never wanted.
text.whitespace: Leading/trailing should be trimmed; collapse runs of 2+ internal spaces to one; never allow tab/newline/NBSP/zero-width inside the value.
text.charset: Extended FIN-X plus !#$&%*=^_`{|}~";<>@[\]. The characters & < > MUST be written as & < >. Smart quotes/dashes/ellipsis must be normalised to ASCII equivalents.

character_blocklist._doc: Catalogue of individual characters/sequences that commonly contaminate messages, with the code point, why it breaks things, and the deterministic fix. 'escape' = replace with XML entity; 'strip' = delete; 'transliterate' = replace with ASCII equivalent; 'context' = depends on field_class.

xml_special_five.name: ampersand
xml_special_five.breaks: Starts an entity reference; a bare & is a fatal well-formedness error unless it begins a valid entity.
xml_special_five.note: Do NOT double-escape an already-correct &/</>/"/' or a valid numeric reference &#nnn;.

xml_special_five.name: less-than
xml_special_five.breaks: Opens a tag; a literal < inside text/attribute content is fatal.

xml_special_five.name: greater-than
xml_special_five.breaks: Required to be escaped in text per CBPR+ and after ']]'; a literal > is unsafe.

xml_special_five.name: double-quote
xml_special_five.breaks: Inside a double-quoted attribute value it terminates the value prematurely.
xml_special_five.note: Only an issue inside attribute values; in element text a literal " is legal but CBPR+ text fields treat it as part of the extended set.

xml_special_five.name: apostrophe
xml_special_five.breaks: Inside a single-quoted attribute value it terminates the value; legal in element text (FIN-X allows it).

html_entities_misused.breaks: Undefined entity in XML (only the five predefined exist).
html_entities_misused.replace_with: a normal space ' ' or   if a non-breaking space is truly intended (but NBSP should usually be stripped from financial fields).
ASCII equivalent ('-', '...', '(c)', etc.) or numeric character reference.

html_entities_misused.sequence: & followed by space or non-entity text

smart_and_typographic.name: acute accent / grave accent (backtick)
smart_and_typographic.replace_with: ASCII apostrophe ' in identifier/strict fields; backtick ` is in the extended text set but is almost always a stray character — strip unless clearly intended.

invisible_and_control.breaks: Legal only as the leading byte-order mark; anywhere else it is an invisible character that corrupts tokens.
Looks like a space, is not a space; contaminates strict tokens and amounts.
invisible_and_control.replace_with: strip in strict_token/numeric/datetime; convert to normal space in text fields
strip in strict fields; collapse in text

invisible_and_control.char: Tab / vertical tab / form feed inside a value
invisible_and_control.breaks: U+000B and U+000C are illegal XML 1.0 characters; tab inside a strict value is contamination.
invisible_and_control.replace_with: strip from strict/numeric/datetime; collapse to space in text. U+000B/U+000C must always be stripped.

invisible_and_control.breaks: Illegal in XML 1.0 entirely; will not parse.
Discouraged/illegal; usually mojibake from a Latin-1 → UTF-8 mis-decode.
Indicates an earlier decoding failure; the real character was lost.
invisible_and_control.replace_with: re-decode from source bytes if possible; otherwise strip and flag for human review.

stray_punctuation_in_strict_fields.breaks: A grouping/decimal comma in an amount, or a stray comma in a BIC/IBAN/date, is a lexical fault.
Outside the FIN-X set for these field classes (some are valid ONLY in extended text fields).
stray_punctuation_in_strict_fields.fix: strip or transliterate; if the character is one of & < > it must instead be escaped

xml_wellformedness_errors._doc: Parser-fatal structural faults. These prevent the document from parsing at all, so they must be fixed before anything else downstream.

WF_UNESCAPED_AMPERSAND.root_cause: A literal & that does not start a valid entity (e.g. 'Smith & Co', 'a&b').
WF_UNESCAPED_AMPERSAND.fix: Replace the bare & with &, preserving surrounding text. Do not touch already-valid entities.

WF_UNESCAPED_LT.root_cause: A literal < inside element text or an attribute value (e.g. 'qty < 10').

WF_UNESCAPED_GT.root_cause: A literal > inside text where CBPR+ requires escaping.

WF_UNESCAPED_QUOTE_IN_ATTR.root_cause: A " inside a double-quoted attribute value, or a ' inside a single-quoted attribute value.
WF_UNESCAPED_QUOTE_IN_ATTR.fix: Escape as " / ', or switch the attribute's delimiter to the other quote style.

WF_UNDEFINED_ENTITY.root_cause: An entity reference other than the five predefined ones (e.g.  , —, &foo;).
WF_UNDEFINED_ENTITY.fix: Replace HTML/custom entities with their literal ASCII or a numeric character reference (  etc.); escape a stray & as &.

WF_MALFORMED_ENTITY.root_cause: An entity started with & but never terminated with ; (e.g. '&amp ' or '&#x' truncated).
WF_MALFORMED_ENTITY.fix: Terminate the entity with ';' or escape the bare & as &.

WF_INVALID_CHAR_REFERENCE.root_cause: A numeric character reference pointing to a code point illegal in XML (e.g. �  ).
WF_INVALID_CHAR_REFERENCE.fix: Remove the reference; XML 1.0 forbids these code points even as references.

WF_UNCLOSED_TAG.root_cause: A start tag with no matching end tag before its parent closes (e.g. <Amt>100.00 missing </Amt>).
WF_UNCLOSED_TAG.fix: Insert the matching end tag immediately before the conflicting closing tag named in the error message. The lxml parser names the unclosed tag and the line of the conflicting close — use both to place </X> precisely. Self-close only if the element is genuinely empty and the schema permits.

WF_OPEN_TAG_SWALLOWED.root_cause: A start tag's '>' was deleted along with the element's content and its own end tag, leaving '<TagName' run directly into whitespace/newline then '/OtherTag>' (a sibling/parent close tag missing its '<'). e.g. '<Ustrd\n            /RmtInf></DrctDbtTxInf>'. lxml reports 'error parsing attribute name' because '<TagName' has no '>' and the text after the stray '/' looks like a bogus attribute.
WF_OPEN_TAG_SWALLOWED.detect: Parser error 'error parsing attribute name' (or 'expected attribute name'). The line contains '<TagName' with no '>' before end-of-line, followed on the next line by '/OtherTag>'.
WF_OPEN_TAG_SWALLOWED.fix: Nothing recoverable remains of <TagName>'s content — collapse to an empty self-closing element and restore the '<' on the close tag that follows: '<TagName/></OtherTag>'. The now-empty element may then fail schema validation if its type forbids empty content (e.g. Max140Text minLength=1) — fix that as a normal, separate content-population step in the next round.

WF_MISSING_OPENING_TAG.root_cause: A closing tag </X> appears in the document but the corresponding opening tag <X> was never written. This is the inverse of WF_UNCLOSED_TAG. Common in CBPR+ messages when the opening tag of a structural container (AppHdr, Document, GrpHdr, TxInf, Ntfctn, Ntry, Acct, BkTxCd, Fr, To, FinInstnId, PstlAdr, etc.) is accidentally deleted while its closing tag remains. The XML parser reports this as 'Unclosed tag <PARENT> ... before the closing tag </X>'.
WF_MISSING_OPENING_TAG.detect: Parser error says 'Unclosed tag <PARENT> ... before the closing tag </X> at line N'. Confirm that <X> (without attributes) does NOT appear anywhere earlier in the document. If <X> is absent, this is WF_MISSING_OPENING_TAG; if it is present but mis-nested, it is WF_OVERLAPPING_TAGS.
WF_MISSING_OPENING_TAG.fix: Use indentation depth to locate the insertion point: (1) measure the indentation of </X> at line N — this is the expected child-indent of X's parent; (2) scan backward to find the parent element (first content line with less indentation); (3) scan forward from the parent to the first content line after it — that is where <X> belongs. Add xmlns only for namespace-declaring elements: AppHdr → xmlns='urn:iso:std:iso:20022:tech:xsd:head.001.001.02'; Document → xmlns='urn:iso:std:iso:20022:tech:xsd:<MsgDefIdr_value>'. All other elements inherit the parent namespace — no xmlns attribute needed.
examples: Missing <GrpHdr> — insert before <MsgId>; no xmlns (inherits Document namespace)
Missing <Fr> or <To> — insert before <FIId>; no xmlns

WF_MISMATCHED_TAG.root_cause: End tag name differs from the start tag, including CASE differences (XML is case-sensitive): <Amt>...</amt>, <BICFI>...</Bicfi>.
WF_MISMATCHED_TAG.fix: Make the end tag exactly match the start tag's name and case.

WF_OVERLAPPING_TAGS.fix: Re-order close tags so elements nest strictly (close the most recently opened first).

WF_ATTR_NOT_QUOTED.fix: Wrap the value in double quotes: Ccy="USD".

WF_ATTR_MISMATCHED_QUOTES.root_cause: Opening and closing quote characters differ (Ccy="USD').
WF_ATTR_MISMATCHED_QUOTES.fix: Use matching double quotes on both sides.

WF_DUPLICATE_ATTRIBUTE.root_cause: The same attribute name appears twice on one element (Ccy="USD" Ccy="EUR").
WF_DUPLICATE_ATTRIBUTE.fix: Keep the correct single occurrence; remove the duplicate.

WF_INVALID_TAG_NAME.root_cause: Element/attribute name starts with a digit, contains a space, or contains an illegal character (e.g. <2Amt>, <Amt Foo>).
WF_INVALID_TAG_NAME.fix: Correct the name to a legal XML Name; in ISO 20022 this almost always means a typo to repair against the schema element name.

WF_STRAY_TEXT_BETWEEN_ELEMENTS.root_cause: Unexpected text nodes between child elements where only elements are allowed (e.g. stray punctuation like ,.?"{}; typed or pasted after a closing tag inside an element-only container such as <Document> or <FIToFIPmtStsRpt>). The parser records this as element.tail or parent.text, and the XSD schema rejects it with 'Character content other than whitespace is not allowed because the content type is element-only'.
WF_STRAY_TEXT_BETWEEN_ELEMENTS.detect: XSD error 'Character content other than whitespace is not allowed' on the named container; inspect child.tail and parent.text for non-whitespace.
WF_STRAY_TEXT_BETWEEN_ELEMENTS.fix: Strip every non-whitespace child.tail inside the offending container and clear parent.text if it is non-whitespace. Set these to None (not to an empty string). Do NOT remove or modify child elements.
WF_STRAY_TEXT_BETWEEN_ELEMENTS.do_not: Do not escape the stray characters — they are structural noise. Do not remove child elements.

WF_TEXT_BEFORE_PROLOG.root_cause: Any character (space, blank line, BOM-as-text, stray text) before the '<?xml' declaration.
WF_TEXT_BEFORE_PROLOG.fix: Delete everything before '<?xml' (or before the first '<' if no declaration). The declaration must be the very first content.

WF_MALFORMED_DECLARATION.root_cause: Broken XML declaration: missing '?', wrong order, version!=1.0, or encoding token malformed.

WF_MULTIPLE_ROOT_ELEMENTS.root_cause: More than one top-level element, or content after the root element's close tag.
WF_MULTIPLE_ROOT_ELEMENTS.fix: Ensure exactly one root element (e.g. <BusMsgEnvlp>...</BusMsgEnvlp>); remove or re-parent stray top-level content; delete trailing garbage after the final close tag.

WF_UNCLOSED_COMMENT.root_cause: A comment opened with <!-- but not closed, or containing '--' inside.
WF_UNCLOSED_COMMENT.fix: Close the comment with -->, remove internal '--', or delete the comment entirely (comments are not needed in production messages).

WF_UNCLOSED_CDATA.root_cause: A CDATA section opened with <![CDATA[ but not closed with ]]>, or a stray ]]> in content.
WF_UNCLOSED_CDATA.fix: Close the CDATA, or remove CDATA wrapping (ISO 20022 messages do not use CDATA) and escape the content normally.

WF_PROCESSING_INSTRUCTION_MISUSE.root_cause: A malformed or unexpected processing instruction.
WF_PROCESSING_INSTRUCTION_MISUSE.fix: Remove it; ISO 20022 business messages should contain only the XML declaration as a PI.

DTD_FORBIDDEN.root_cause: A DOCTYPE declaration (<!DOCTYPE ...>) is present. ISO 20022 CBPR+ messages must not contain DTD declarations. Parsers with DTD processing enabled are vulnerable to XXE (XML External Entity) injection.
DTD_FORBIDDEN.fix: Remove the entire <!DOCTYPE ...> block (including all ELEMENT, ATTLIST, and ENTITY declarations within it). Do not relocate it; delete completely.

ENTITY_FORBIDDEN.root_cause: A custom entity declaration (<!ENTITY ...>) is present. Custom entities are forbidden. They can be used for entity expansion (Billion Laughs) DoS attacks.
ENTITY_FORBIDDEN.fix: Remove the <!ENTITY ...> declaration. Replace any &entityname; references in the content with their literal text values.

encoding_and_invisible_chars._doc: Byte- and encoding-level faults that either stop parsing or silently corrupt values.

ENC_BOM_PRESENT.root_cause: A UTF-8 BOM (EF BB BF) precedes the XML declaration.
ENC_BOM_PRESENT.fix: Many parsers tolerate a leading UTF-8 BOM, but some SWIFT/MQ pipelines reject it. Strip the leading BOM unless the receiving system explicitly requires it. A BOM anywhere other than the first bytes is always an error (see ENC_ZWNBSP_INLINE).

ENC_WRONG_BOM.root_cause: A UTF-16/UTF-32 BOM (FF FE / FE FF / 00 00 FE FF) on a document declared UTF-8.
ENC_WRONG_BOM.fix: Re-encode the document to UTF-8 without BOM and align the encoding declaration.

ENC_DECLARATION_MISMATCH.root_cause: The declaration says encoding="UTF-8" but the bytes are actually Latin-1/Windows-1252 (typical symptom: accented letters appear as two garbled characters, e.g. 'Ã¼' for 'ü').
ENC_DECLARATION_MISMATCH.fix: Re-decode the bytes from their true encoding and re-save as UTF-8, OR correct the encoding declaration to match the real bytes. Verify by checking that accented names render correctly afterwards.

ENC_INVALID_UTF8_SEQUENCE.root_cause: Byte sequences that are not valid UTF-8 (lone continuation bytes, overlong encodings).
ENC_INVALID_UTF8_SEQUENCE.fix: Re-decode from the source encoding; if unknown, strip the offending bytes and flag for human review (data loss risk).

ENC_ILLEGAL_CONTROL_CHAR.root_cause: A C0 control character (U+0000–U+0008, U+000B, U+000C, U+000E–U+001F) appears in the document; these are illegal in XML 1.0 and the parser will reject the file.
ENC_ILLEGAL_CONTROL_CHAR.fix: Strip the character. If it sits inside a value, ensure the surrounding text still reads correctly.

ENC_C1_CONTROL_CHAR.fix: Strip, or re-decode if part of a mis-decoded multibyte sequence.

ENC_ZWNBSP_INLINE.root_cause: U+FEFF appearing inside the document body rather than as the leading BOM.
ENC_ZWNBSP_INLINE.fix: Strip every inline U+FEFF; it is an invisible character that splits tokens.

ENC_REPLACEMENT_CHAR.root_cause: U+FFFD present, marking a character lost in an earlier decode.
ENC_REPLACEMENT_CHAR.fix: Re-decode from original bytes if available; otherwise strip and flag — the original character cannot be recovered from U+FFFD.

whitespace_errors._doc: Whitespace contamination by field_class. The most common real-world cause is copy-paste and XML pretty-printing leaking indentation into element text.

WS_LEADING_TRAILING.root_cause: A value has leading or trailing spaces/tabs/newlines (e.g. <BICFI> DEUTDEFFXXX </BICFI>).
WS_LEADING_TRAILING.fix: Trim leading and trailing whitespace. For strict_token/numeric/datetime there must be ZERO whitespace; for text, trim outer whitespace.

WS_PRETTYPRINT_LEAKAGE.root_cause: A newline + indentation was captured as the element's text because the value was placed on its own line and indented (e.g. <MsgId>\n        B123\n      </MsgId>).
WS_PRETTYPRINT_LEAKAGE.fix: Collapse the element to a single line with no surrounding whitespace: <MsgId>B123</MsgId>. Critical for strict tokens — the leaked whitespace makes the value invalid.

WS_INTERNAL_IN_TOKEN.root_cause: Whitespace inside a strict token (BIC 'DEUT DEFF XXX', IBAN 'DE89 3704 0044', amount '1 000.00', date '2026 -06-01', code 'IN GA').
WS_INTERNAL_IN_TOKEN.fix: Remove ALL internal whitespace, rejoining the token. 'DEUT DEFF XXX' → 'DEUTDEFFXXX'; 'DE89 3704 0044' → 'DE8937040044'.

WS_MULTIPLE_SPACES_IN_TEXT.root_cause: Runs of 2+ spaces inside a name/address (often from tab expansion or merged fields).
WS_MULTIPLE_SPACES_IN_TEXT.fix: Collapse internal runs of whitespace to a single ASCII space.

WS_TAB_OR_NEWLINE_IN_VALUE.root_cause: A tab or newline embedded inside a value.
WS_TAB_OR_NEWLINE_IN_VALUE.fix: Strip from strict/numeric/datetime; replace with a single space in text fields, then collapse.

WS_EMPTY_OR_WHITESPACE_ONLY.root_cause: An element present but empty or containing only whitespace (e.g. <Ccy></Ccy>, <BkTxCd>   </BkTxCd>) where content is required.
WS_EMPTY_OR_WHITESPACE_ONLY.fix: This KB removes the whitespace and FLAGS the element as effectively empty; the decision of what value belongs there (or whether to delete the element) is a business question — hand off to the global KB (MISSING_MANDATORY_FIELD / MISSING_EXPECTED_ELEMENT). Do not invent a value here.

numeric_amount_syntax_errors._doc: Amounts/rates/numbers must be a plain decimal with a single dot and no decoration. These are among the most frequent real-world faults (locale formatting leaking from spreadsheets).

NUM_THOUSANDS_SEPARATOR_COMMA.root_cause: Anglo grouping commas in an amount (e.g. '1,200.00', '10,000,000.00').
NUM_THOUSANDS_SEPARATOR_COMMA.fix: Remove every grouping comma, keeping the dot decimal: '1,200.00' → '1200.00'.
NUM_THOUSANDS_SEPARATOR_COMMA.do_not: Do not confuse the grouping comma with a decimal comma — see the European case.

NUM_DECIMAL_COMMA.root_cause: European decimal comma (e.g. '1200,50' or '1.200,50' meaning one-thousand-two-hundred and fifty).
NUM_DECIMAL_COMMA.fix: If the value matches '#.###,##' (dot groups + comma decimal), remove dots and convert the comma to a dot: '1.200,50' → '1200.50'. If the value is simply 'NNN,NN', convert the comma to a dot: '1200,50' → '1200.50'.
NUM_DECIMAL_COMMA.disambiguation: Decide grouping-vs-decimal by position: a separator followed by exactly 2 digits at the end is the decimal mark; separators every 3 digits are grouping.

NUM_CURRENCY_SYMBOL.root_cause: A currency symbol or code embedded in the amount text ('$1200.00', '€1.200,00', '1200.00 USD', 'USD1200').
NUM_CURRENCY_SYMBOL.fix: Strip the symbol/letters from the amount NODE. The currency belongs only in the Ccy ATTRIBUTE: <Amt Ccy="USD">1200.00</Amt>. If the embedded code conflicts with the existing Ccy attribute, flag for review rather than guessing.

NUM_INTERNAL_SPACE.fix: Remove all spaces (including NBSP/thin spaces), then apply the decimal-separator rule: '1 200,00' → '1200.00'.

NUM_TYPOGRAPHIC_MINUS.root_cause: A Unicode minus U+2212 or dash instead of ASCII '-' on a negative value.
NUM_TYPOGRAPHIC_MINUS.fix: Replace with ASCII '-'. (Whether a negative is even allowed is a schema/business matter — hand off.)

NUM_MULTIPLE_DECIMAL_POINTS.root_cause: More than one '.' ('1.200.50' from a botched locale conversion).
NUM_MULTIPLE_DECIMAL_POINTS.fix: Interpret using grouping/decimal disambiguation and reduce to a single decimal point: '1.200.50' → '1200.50'.

NUM_TRAILING_DOT_OR_BARE.root_cause: Trailing decimal point ('1200.') or naked separator.
NUM_TRAILING_DOT_OR_BARE.fix: Remove a trailing dot ('1200.' → '1200'); add nothing else.

NUM_NON_DIGIT_CHARS.root_cause: Stray letters/symbols mixed into a number ('12O0.00' with letter O, '1200.00*').
NUM_NON_DIGIT_CHARS.fix: Correct obvious OCR/typo confusions (letter O → digit 0, letter l → digit 1) only when unambiguous; otherwise strip trailing symbols and flag.

numeric_amount_syntax_errors._handoff_note: After lexical normalisation, decimal-place COUNT versus the currency's minor unit (e.g. USD max 2, JPY 0) is a BUSINESS rule — hand off to the global KB (R12 / D00007). This KB only fixes the lexical form.

datetime_lexical_errors._doc: LEXICAL shape of dates/datetimes only. The Z-suffix, milliseconds, and offset-presence rules are owned by the GLOBAL KB (CBPR_DATETIME_Z_FORBIDDEN / CBPR_DATETIME_MILLISECONDS / CBPR_DATETIME_NO_TIMEZONE) and must NOT be re-decided here — only cross-referenced.

DT_WRONG_DATE_SEPARATOR.fix: Convert to YYYY-MM-DD with hyphens. If the order is also wrong (DD/MM/YYYY or MM/DD/YYYY), reorder to YYYY-MM-DD — but flag ambiguous DD-vs-MM cases for review rather than guessing.

DT_SPACE_INSTEAD_OF_T.root_cause: Date and time separated by a space instead of 'T' ('2026-06-01 06:21:38+00:00').

DT_MISSING_T.root_cause: Date and time concatenated with no separator ('2026-06-0106:21:38').
DT_MISSING_T.fix: Insert 'T' between the date and time components.

DT_INTERNAL_SPACE.root_cause: Stray spaces inside the value ('2026-06-01 T 06:21:38', '06 :21:38').

DT_TRAILING_GARBAGE.root_cause: Trailing characters after the datetime ('2026-06-01T06:21:38+00:00Z', a stray comma, or text).
DT_TRAILING_GARBAGE.fix: Remove trailing garbage. NOTE: a trailing 'Z' alongside an offset, or a 'Z' suffix generally, is the GLOBAL KB's call (CBPR_DATETIME_Z_FORBIDDEN) — strip only obviously stray characters here and hand off the Z/offset decision.

namespace_and_attribute_syntax_errors._doc: Prefix/namespace and attribute lexical faults that block parsing or schema location.

NS_UNDECLARED_PREFIX.root_cause: An element/attribute uses a namespace prefix that was never declared with xmlns:prefix (e.g. <ns2:Amt> with no xmlns:ns2).
NS_UNDECLARED_PREFIX.fix: Either declare the prefix on an ancestor (xmlns:ns2="...the correct ISO namespace...") or remove the prefix if the default namespace already applies. For ISO 20022, the Document namespace is the message URI (e.g. urn:iso:std:iso:20022:tech:xsd:camt.052.001.08).

NS_PREFIX_MISMATCH_ON_CLOSE.root_cause: Close tag prefix differs from the open tag (<ns2:Amt>...</ns3:Amt>).
NS_PREFIX_MISMATCH_ON_CLOSE.fix: Make the close-tag prefix identical to the open-tag prefix.

NS_MISSING_DEFAULT_NAMESPACE.root_cause: The AppHdr or Document element lacks its xmlns default declaration, so children are in no namespace and the schema cannot bind.
NS_MISSING_DEFAULT_NAMESPACE.fix: Restore the correct default namespace on AppHdr (urn:iso:std:iso:20022:tech:xsd:head.001.001.02) and Document (the message URI). NOTE: the exact URI/version is a SCHEMA matter — confirm against the global KB's MsgDefIdr/namespace mapping; this KB only flags the missing/malformed declaration syntax.

NS_TYPO_IN_URI.root_cause: A typo in the namespace URI (e.g. 'urn:iso:std:iso:20022:tech:xsd:camt.052.001.8' missing a zero, or 'xds' for 'xsd').
NS_TYPO_IN_URI.fix: Correct the URI string to the exact, well-formed namespace token. Cross-check the message-id portion against the global KB.

ATTR_CCY_LEXICAL.root_cause: The Ccy attribute has stray whitespace or lowercase ('Ccy=" usd "', 'Ccy="usd"').
ATTR_CCY_LEXICAL.fix: Trim whitespace and upper-case to 3 letters: Ccy="USD". (Whether 'USD' is a VALID ISO 4217 code is a business check — hand off; this KB only fixes spacing/casing of the token.)

ATTR_STRAY_CHARS.root_cause: Stray characters or smart quotes around an attribute value (Ccy=“USD” using curly quotes).
ATTR_STRAY_CHARS.fix: Replace curly quotes with straight ASCII double quotes; remove stray characters.

error_code_catalogue._doc: Flat lookup of every syntactic error code in this KB → one-line root cause + fix. The fixer checks THIS catalogue for any parser/lexical error and only falls through to the global business catalogue for element/codelist/dependency errors.

WF_UNESCAPED_AMPERSAND.root_cause: Bare & not starting a valid entity.

WF_UNESCAPED_QUOTE_IN_ATTR.root_cause: Active quote char inside an attribute value.

WF_UNDEFINED_ENTITY.fix: Replace with literal/numeric reference; escape stray & as &.

WF_INVALID_CHAR_REFERENCE.root_cause: Numeric reference to an XML-illegal code point.

WF_UNCLOSED_TAG.root_cause: Start tag with no matching end tag.
WF_UNCLOSED_TAG.fix: Insert the matching end tag immediately before the conflicting closing tag named in the parser error.

WF_OPEN_TAG_SWALLOWED.root_cause: Start tag's '>' deleted along with its content and end tag, run directly into a sibling close tag missing its '<' (e.g. '<Ustrd\n  /RmtInf>'). lxml reports 'error parsing attribute name'.
WF_OPEN_TAG_SWALLOWED.fix: Collapse to '<TagName/></OtherTag>' (empty self-close + restored close tag). Populate the now-empty element in a later round if schema requires non-empty content.

WF_MISSING_OPENING_TAG.root_cause: Closing tag </X> present but opening <X> is absent (inverse of WF_UNCLOSED_TAG).
WF_MISSING_OPENING_TAG.fix: Scan backward from </X> to find the parent (first line with less indentation), then forward to the first content line after the parent — insert <X [xmlns='...']> there. Add xmlns for AppHdr (head.001.001.02) and Document (message-type URI); omit xmlns for all other elements.

WF_MISMATCHED_TAG.root_cause: End tag name/case differs from start tag.

WF_DUPLICATE_ATTRIBUTE.root_cause: Same attribute twice on one element.

WF_INVALID_TAG_NAME.fix: Repair to the legal schema name.

WF_STRAY_CHAR_IN_TAG.root_cause: Illegal character inside a tag opening/closing (e.g. '!' in '<BusMsgEnvlp xmlns="..."!>' or in '<BusMsgEnvlp!>'). The character appears AFTER the closing quote of the last attribute value but BEFORE the closing '>' of the tag.
WF_STRAY_CHAR_IN_TAG.fix: Strip the stray character(s) between the last attribute quote and the closing '>'. Example: '<BusMsgEnvlp xmlns="urn:swift:xsd:envelope"!>' → '<BusMsgEnvlp xmlns="urn:swift:xsd:envelope">'. Pattern: remove any non-whitespace, non-'>' characters that appear after the last '"' or "'" in a tag but before its closing '>'.
WF_STRAY_CHAR_IN_TAG.applies_to: all message types — pacs.008, pacs.009, pacs.002, pacs.003, pacs.004, pacs.010, pain.001, pain.002, pain.008, camt.052, camt.053, camt.054, camt.055, camt.056, camt.057

WF_STRAY_CHAR_IN_SELF_CLOSE_TAG.root_cause: Stray character before '/>' in a self-closing tag (e.g. '<BICFI!/>') or before '>' in an opening tag with no attributes (e.g. '<Document!>').

WF_MULTIPLE_ROOT_ELEMENTS.root_cause: More than one root / trailing content.
WF_MULTIPLE_ROOT_ELEMENTS.fix: Keep one root; remove trailing garbage.

WF_UNCLOSED_COMMENT.fix: Close with --> or delete the comment.

WF_UNCLOSED_CDATA.fix: Close or remove CDATA; escape content normally.

ENC_BOM_PRESENT.fix: Strip unless the receiver requires it.

ENC_WRONG_BOM.root_cause: UTF-16/32 BOM on a UTF-8 doc.

ENC_DECLARATION_MISMATCH.fix: Re-decode/re-save as UTF-8 or fix the declaration.

ENC_INVALID_UTF8_SEQUENCE.fix: Re-decode from source; else strip + flag.

ENC_ILLEGAL_CONTROL_CHAR.root_cause: C0 control char illegal in XML 1.0.

ENC_REPLACEMENT_CHAR.fix: Re-decode if possible; else strip + flag.

LEX_STRAY_ACCENT_BACKTICK.root_cause: Acute/grave accent or backtick used as apostrophe.
LEX_STRAY_ACCENT_BACKTICK.fix: Replace with ASCII ' in ID fields; strip stray backticks.

LEX_NBSP.fix: Strip in strict fields; convert to normal space in text.

LEX_EXOTIC_SPACE.fix: Strip in strict fields; collapse in text.

LEX_CONTROL_WHITESPACE.fix: Strip from strict; collapse to space in text; always strip VT/FF.

LEX_STRAY_COMMA.root_cause: Comma where the field grammar forbids it.

LEX_DISALLOWED_SYMBOL.root_cause: Symbol outside the field-class charset (@ # % * = ^ _ { } | ~ ; [ ] \ ` $ ! in strict/identifier fields).
LEX_DISALLOWED_SYMBOL.fix: Strip or transliterate; if it is & < > escape instead.

WS_PRETTYPRINT_LEAKAGE.fix: Collapse element to one line, no surrounding whitespace.

WS_MULTIPLE_SPACES_IN_TEXT.root_cause: Runs of spaces in a name/address.

WS_EMPTY_OR_WHITESPACE_ONLY.root_cause: Element empty or whitespace-only where content is required.
WS_EMPTY_OR_WHITESPACE_ONLY.fix: Strip whitespace and FLAG; hand the missing-value decision to the global KB.

NUM_THOUSANDS_SEPARATOR_COMMA.fix: Remove grouping commas, keep dot decimal.

NUM_DECIMAL_COMMA.fix: Remove dot groups, convert comma to dot.

NUM_CURRENCY_SYMBOL.root_cause: Currency symbol/code inside the amount node.
NUM_CURRENCY_SYMBOL.fix: Strip from node; currency lives only in the Ccy attribute.

NUM_INTERNAL_SPACE.fix: Remove spaces, then fix decimal mark.

NUM_MULTIPLE_DECIMAL_POINTS.fix: Reduce to a single decimal point.

NUM_NON_DIGIT_CHARS.fix: Fix unambiguous OCR confusions; else strip + flag.

DT_TRAILING_GARBAGE.fix: Remove stray trailing chars; hand off Z/offset decisions to the global KB.

NS_UNDECLARED_PREFIX.fix: Declare it or drop it in favour of the default namespace.

NS_MISSING_DEFAULT_NAMESPACE.fix: Restore the correct default namespace (verify URI via global KB).

ATTR_STRAY_CHARS.root_cause: Smart quotes/stray chars around an attribute.
ATTR_STRAY_CHARS.fix: Use straight ASCII quotes; remove stray chars.

SCHEMA_VAL_STRAY_TEXT.root_cause: Non-whitespace character content (e.g. stray punctuation like ',.?"' '{}' or a word typed by mistake) appears directly inside an element whose XSD content type is 'element-only' (e.g. <Document>, <FIToFIPmtStsRpt>, <GrpHdr>). These characters become a text node or a child-tail in the parsed tree and the schema rejects them with 'Character content other than whitespace is not allowed because the content type is element-only'. Common cause: the user typed or pasted special characters next to a closing tag in the editor.
SCHEMA_VAL_STRAY_TEXT.detect: lxml/XSD validation emits: "Character content other than whitespace is not allowed because the content type is 'element-only'" for the named container element.
SCHEMA_VAL_STRAY_TEXT.fix: Locate the named container element and strip every non-whitespace text node: (1) set container.text = None if it is non-whitespace; (2) for each direct child element, set child.tail = None if it is non-whitespace. Do NOT remove child elements or change their content — only the stray inter-element text is removed.
SCHEMA_VAL_STRAY_TEXT.do_not: Do not remove child elements or insert new ones. Do not escape the stray characters — they are structural noise and must be deleted entirely.
examples: </FIToFIPmtStsRpt> ,.?"} <-- stray chars become FIToFIPmtStsRpt.tail inside Document
<Document>\n  some text\n  <FIToFICstmrCdtTrf> <-- text before first child

WF_STRAY_TEXT_AFTER_CLOSE_TAG.root_cause: Characters typed or pasted after a closing tag but before the parent's closing tag (e.g. </FIToFIPmtStsRpt> ,.?"} </Document>). The parser records these as the tail of the child element, which lands as character content inside the parent — a schema violation for element-only parents.
WF_STRAY_TEXT_AFTER_CLOSE_TAG.detect: The XSD validator reports 'Character content other than whitespace is not allowed' on the parent; inspecting child.tail values reveals the stray text.
WF_STRAY_TEXT_AFTER_CLOSE_TAG.fix: Strip the tail of each child element whose tail contains non-whitespace characters. Set child.tail = None (or a clean newline/indent if the document is pretty-printed).
WF_STRAY_TEXT_AFTER_CLOSE_TAG.do_not: Do not escape the tail text — it is not content that belongs in the message.

DTD_FORBIDDEN.root_cause: DOCTYPE declaration present. Forbidden in ISO 20022.

ENTITY_FORBIDDEN.root_cause: Entity declaration present. Forbidden in ISO 20022.
ENTITY_FORBIDDEN.fix: Remove <!ENTITY ...> and replace entity references with literal values.

transliteration_map._doc: Deterministic ASCII replacements for common non-ASCII characters when a field class requires plain ASCII (strict_token, identifier) OR when the global INVALID_CHARSETS rule applies. In CBPR+ TEXT fields (Nm/Adr/RmtInf) accented Latin letters are permitted and need NOT be transliterated — only invisible/smart/zero-width characters are cleaned there.
transliteration_map.note: Use latin_accents_for_strict_fields_only ONLY when the target field class is strict_token/identifier, or when the validator raised the global INVALID_CHARSETS code for a field that does not permit accents. NEVER transliterate accents inside CBPR+ Nm/AdrLine/Ustrd text fields just because they are non-ASCII — they are valid there.

escaping_rules._doc: The ONLY five characters that have XML entity escapes. Everything else is either a literal, a numeric character reference, or must be stripped/transliterated.
when_to_escape: & — ALWAYS escape in both text and attribute values unless it already begins a valid entity.
< — ALWAYS escape in text and attribute values.
> — escape in text (CBPR+ requires it; XML strictly requires it only after ']]').
" — escape inside double-quoted attribute values (optional in element text).
' — escape inside single-quoted attribute values (legal as a literal in element text and in FIN-X identifier fields).
escaping_rules.idempotency_guard: Before escaping, detect existing valid entities (& < > " ' &#nnn; &#xHH;) and skip them, so the fixer never produces &amp;.
do_not: Do NOT use HTML entities (  — © ...) — they are undefined in XML.
Do NOT escape characters that are not one of the five (e.g. do not turn @ into an entity — either it is allowed in the field, or it should be stripped).
Do NOT wrap values in CDATA to avoid escaping — ISO 20022 messages do not use CDATA.

worked_examples._doc: Concrete before/after pairs spanning the categories, for the fixer to pattern-match against. Each shows ONLY the syntactic repair this KB is responsible for.

at_symbol_in_msgid.note: @ and # are outside the FIN-X identifier set; strip them (do not escape — escaping only applies to & < > " ').

guardrails._doc: Hard rules to stop the fixer from causing damage while repairing syntax.
rules: PRESERVE INTENT: a syntax fix must keep the original human-readable content. Removing a thousands comma must not change the numeric value; escaping & must not delete 'Co'.

NO BUSINESS INVENTION: never substitute a dummy BIC/IBAN/code/amount to make a syntactically broken value 'valid'. If a value is unrecoverable, strip the contamination and flag for the global KB / human review.
IDEMPOTENT ESCAPING: never double-escape; detect existing valid entities first.
DISAMBIGUATE NUMBERS CAREFULLY: when a separator could be grouping or decimal, decide by the 3-digit grouping vs 2-digit-tail heuristic; if still ambiguous, flag rather than guess.
DATETIME HAND-OFF: fix only separators/spacing here; never add, remove, or rewrite the 'Z'/offset/milliseconds — that is the global KB's CBPR_DATETIME_* domain.
ACCENTS IN TEXT FIELDS: do not transliterate valid accented Latin letters inside CBPR+ Nm/Adr/RmtInf; only clean invisible/smart/zero-width characters there.
ONE FAULT, ONE FIX: report and fix each syntactic fault independently; do not bundle a syntactic fix with a business fix.
REVALIDATE: after applying this KB's fixes, the document MUST be well-formed XML before the global business KB is consulted.
